chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hammad ibn Uthman from Udaym ibn al-Harr who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man should not perform voluntary prayer when the time for the obligatory prayer has entered.'
He said, and he said: 'When the time for the obligatory prayer has entered, begin with it.'

The Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And the traveler, if he fears that sleep will overcome him due to the fatigue he has incurred, and he will not stand [in prayer] in the latter part of the night, then let him advance the prayer of his night in its beginning, after the last 'Isha prayer, up to the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): 'And whoever is weak from the night prayer while standing.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing voluntary prayers when the time for obligatory prayer has entered, and how should travelers handle night prayer if they fear sleep?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of prioritizing obligatory prayers over voluntary ones once their specific time enters, a ruling derived from the general Quranic injunction to observe prayers at their appointed times. Shaykh al-Tusi supplements this with a practical legal concession for travelers or the fatigued, permitting them to perform night prayers (Salat al-Layl) early after 'Isha to avoid missing them due to sleep, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with physical capability.
